The new controls reuse an existing local-file drag capability rather than adding privileges or automatic uploads. No introduced security defect was established, but sender-origin enforcement and native drag behavior remain incompletely verified.

**Retained concerns**
No architecture-level concerns identified.

<details>
<summary><strong>Security review details</strong></summary>
<dl>
<dd>

**Security Blast Radius**
- _inferred_ — The affected authority is the desktop user's existing ability to hand local vault files to another application. The new caller makes historical local copies easier to drag but introduces no new IPC capability or demonstrated service, tenant, credential, or deployment authority.

**Trust Boundaries and Controls**
- _observed_ — The renderer supplies an ID and display title, not a filesystem path. Main rejects IDs containing path separators or double dots, resolves the file through the current vault, requires a usable thumbnail, and sanitizes friendly staging names. These controls predate the new caller.
- _observed_ — The drag handler contains no explicit sender-frame or origin validation and is registered directly through the library registration function. This condition and the prior export-ready caller exist at the PR base; no new untrusted sender or broader sender access was established. Application-wide sender-trust enforcement remains a coverage limitation, not an introduced finding.

**Resilience and Maintainability Implications**
- _observed_ — The unchanged staging mechanism uses per-drag UUID directories, normally hard-links the vault file, and scopes pruning and cleanup to drag staging rather than deleting the source. Startup and quit cleanup are gated by the single-instance lifecycle. This separates repeated and concurrent staging operations and provides next-start recovery after interruption; receiving-application writes through hard-link aliases and native drag timing were not runtime-verified.

</dd>
</dl>
</details>
<!-- architecture_review_end -->

</dd>
</dl>
